note: First measurement of a non-Qwen, non-Ollama-community-default model on this host: NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 9B v2, hybrid Mamba-2/attention architecture (~4 attention layers only), downloaded as a community GGUF (unsloth-style Q4_K_L quant, 6.75 GB on disk / ~7.3 GB loaded). At num_ctx=8192, `ollama ps` reported 15%/85% CPU/GPU split (PROCESSOR column) -- NOT fully GPU-resident, unlike every Qwen2.5-Coder entry in this file at comparable size/context. Only 480 MB of the 8 GB card was free once loaded, leaving no room for the KV cache to stay fully resident. gen_tok_s=12.7 sits inside this file's already-documented 10-20x offload cliff (entry 1: fully-resident 7B-class models get 41-52 tok/s; anything that spills gets 1-5 tok/s) -- 12.7 tok/s is partial-spill territory, consistent with a 15% CPU share rather than the much larger spill fractions this file's other partial-offload entries record, which matches a shallower, still-costly spill rather than the full collapse the deepest-offload entries show. prompt_eval_ms/eval_ms are the API's own reported compute durations (isolated from client-side queueing); the raw measurement also queued ~113s behind a concurrently-running harness job before this request was even accepted, which is NOT included in these duration fields and is noted here only so a reader does not mistake this run for a solo, uncontended measurement of Ollama's queueing latency itself. Whether a smaller num_ctx restores full GPU residency for this model (as it did for the qwen num_ctx=16384-to-8192 change made 2026-09-15 for a different reason, see M6's queue notes) is not yet measured -- natural next run for this file.
